**Defense of the answer**

The common folklore that touching a toad will give you warts is a myth. Human warts are caused by infection with human papillomavirus (HPV), a virus that infects only humans. Toads do not carry HPV, nor do they have any mechanism to transmit it to people. While many toads secrete a mild irritant (bufotoxin) from skin glands, this can cause temporary skin irritation if it contacts mucous membranes, but it does not produce warts or any lasting effect on the skin.
